1.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that the people of Israel will **return** to him. The result of this condition comes in the next verse. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [If you are going to return, Israel]
If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **you should return** before the information about **to me**. Alternate translation: [you should return to me]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel repenting and becoming loyal to him again as if they would physically **return** to him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [it is to me that you must repent]

The implication is that these **detestable things** are idols. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [your idols, which are detestable to me]
Here, **my face** represents Yahweh’s own presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from my presence]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Israel being unfaithful to him as if they would **wander** away from him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not turn away from me in unfaithfulness]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **wander**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and remain faithful to me]

2.note: Following the custom of the culture, the people of Israel would swear an oath by declaring that **Yahweh is alive**, so that their promise would be as certain as Yahweh himself. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express the force of this oath in another way. Alternate translation: [and you take an oath, saying, ‘I solemnly swear by Yahweh, who lives forever’]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **truth**, **justice**, and **righteousness**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [speaking honestly, acting fairly, and living uprightly] or [speaking truthfully, acting justly, and living righteously]

Yahweh is using **bless themselves in him** as a common expression of the culture to mean “ask Yahweh to bless them as he has blessed Israel.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [then the nations will ask Yahweh to bless them as he has blessed Israel]

Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person as **him**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [and in me they will boast]

3.note: In this verse, the word **man** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the people of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “man.” Alternate translation: [to the men of Judah]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah preparing themselves to receive his message as if they were farmers breaking up **unplowed ground** so that it could be planted. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Prepare your hardened hearts to receive my word]

Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah wasting their efforts while they remain unrepentant as if they were farmers who would **sow into thorns**, meaning that the farmers would sow their seed in a place where it will not grow. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and do not waste your efforts while you remain unrepentant]

4.note: Yahweh is speaking of the people of Judah dedicating themselves completely to him as if they were to be **circumcised** for him. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Dedicate yourselves completely to Yahweh]

The expression **Be circumcised** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Consecrate yourselves to Yahweh] or [Undergo circumcision to Yahweh]

Yahweh is speaking of the stubbornness of the people of Judah as if it were **the foreskins of your heart** that they should cut away. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and remove your inner stubbornness]

Yahweh is using this possessive form to mean a foreskin that covers the **heart**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the foreskins that cover your heart]
Here, **lest** marks what follows as the outcome that the people of Judah should act in order to avoid. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

4.q: פֶּן־תֵּצֵ֨א כָ⁠אֵ֜שׁ חֲמָתִ֗⁠י וּ⁠בָעֲרָה֙ וְ⁠אֵ֣ין מְכַבֶּ֔ה
4.note: The point of this comparison is that just as a **fire** burns until there is no one able to **extinguish** it, so Yahweh’s anger will burn against the people of Judah and no one will be able to stop it. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [lest my anger break out and burn as unstoppably as a fire, and there will be no one able to quench it]
Here, **my heat** represents Yahweh’s anger. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [my anger]

Yahweh is using **from the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of the evil of your deeds]

5.q: הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽ⁠יהוּדָ֗ה וּ⁠בִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ וְ⁠אִמְר֕וּ ו⁠תקעו שׁוֹפָ֖ר בָּ⁠אָ֑רֶץ קִרְא֤וּ מַלְאוּ֙ וְ⁠אִמְר֔וּ הֵאָסְפ֥וּ וְ⁠נָב֖וֹאָה אֶל־עָרֵ֥י הַ⁠מִּבְצָֽר
5.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [Proclaim loudly throughout Judah and Jerusalem and say, “Blow the horn in the land! Assemble, and let us go into the cities of fortification.”]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Declare this message in Judah, and in Jerusalem announce this message]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and say that they should blow the horn in the land.]

Yahweh is using **Call out fully** as a common expression of the culture to mean “shout loudly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Shout loudly]

6.note: The implication is that this **banner** would be a signal telling people to flee to **Zion**, where they would be safe. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Raise a signal flag to tell people to flee to Zion]

A **banner** is a pole with a flag or another marker on it that people raised up where others could see it in order to signal them. If your readers would not be familiar with what a banner is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [a signal flag]

6.q: כִּ֣י רָעָ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא מִ⁠צָּפ֖וֹן וְ⁠שֶׁ֥בֶר גָּדֽוֹל
6.note: The implication is that Yahweh will bring this **disaster** by means of an enemy army that will invade Judah from **the north**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For I am bringing disaster from the north by means of an invading army that will cause a great breaking]

Yahweh is speaking of the ruin of the nation of Judah as if it were a wall or a building suffering **a great breaking**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and terrible ruin]

7.q: עָלָ֤ה אַרְיֵה֙ מִֽ⁠סֻּבְּכ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠מַשְׁחִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם נָסַ֖ע
7.note: These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Another approach would be to connect the phrases with a word that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. See how you as a team have decided to translate the parallel phrases in poetry, and follow that approach here and throughout this chapter. Alternate translation: [An army that has destroyed many nations has come like a lion out of its thicket and set out to attack]

7.q: עָלָ֤ה אַרְיֵה֙ מִֽ⁠סֻּבְּכ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠מַשְׁחִ֣ית גּוֹיִ֔ם נָסַ֖ע
7.note: Jeremiah is using the past tense to describe something that is going to happen in the future in order to show that the event will certainly happen. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use the future tense. Alternate translation: [A lion is about to come up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations will attack you]

Jeremiah is speaking of the enemy army that will invade Judah as if it were a **lion** that had come up out of its **thicket** to hunt. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A ferocious enemy has come out from its homeland]

The implication is that this **destroyer of nations** is the king of Babylon, who is coming with his army. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and the king of Babylon, who destroys nations, has set out with his army]

8.note: The words translated as **Because of this** indicate that what follows is the result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is the result of what came before. Alternate translation: [As a result, gird yourselves with sackcloth, lament and wail!]

Putting on **sackcloth** was a symbolic action by which people in this culture showed that they were mourning deeply. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [clothe yourselves in sackcloth, the clothing of deep mourning]

The terms **lament** and **wail** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [mourn loudly]

The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]
Yahweh is speaking about himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [my burning anger]

Yahweh is using **the nose of Yahweh** as a common expression of the culture to mean “Yahweh’s anger.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s anger]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word “turned away.” If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [is still directed against us]

Although Yahweh is speaking, he is giving Jeremiah the words to say. So the pronoun **us** refers to Jeremiah along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from us, the people of Judah and Jerusalem]

9.note: Yahweh is speaking of the courage of the king and of his officials as if it were a **heart** that could **perish**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the king and the officials will lose their courage]

10.note: Jeremiah is using a word that expresses a strong feeling of grief and dismay. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh no]
If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [by telling them that they would have peace]

Here, **the sword** represents warfare and killing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Yet deadly warfare will reach as far as the life]

11.note: The expression **it will be said** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [one will say to this people and to Jerusalem]

Yahweh is speaking of the enemy army that will attack the people of Judah as if it were a **searing wind** blowing in from **the bare hills in the wilderness**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [A destructive enemy army coming from the desert region]

Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [this wind is blowing toward my beloved people]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and this wind is coming not for winnowing and not for cleansing her]

Yahweh is speaking of the coming disaster as if it were a wind that is **not to winnow and not to cleanse** grain, unlike the gentle wind that is normally used for that beneficial purpose. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [not a soft breeze used to separate grain from chaff, but a violent, destructive wind] or [not a disaster that will spare the innocent, but one that will destroy everyone]

12.note: Yahweh is speaking of the enemy army that will attack the people of Judah as if it were **a wind** far stronger than any wind that farmers use for winnowing. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a powerful, destructive army will come at my command]

The pronoun **these** refers to the winds that farmers use to winnow and cleanse their grain. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [a wind more full than the winds used for winnowing]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgments**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [I myself shall also speak and judge against my people]

13.note: Jeremiah is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]

The point of this comparison is that just as storm **clouds** rise up and cover the whole sky, so the enemy will advance and overwhelm the whole land. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [he comes up and overwhelms the whole land]

The point of this comparison is that just as **the storm** rushes forward and destroys whatever is in its path, so the enemy’s **chariots** will rush forward and destroy whatever is in their path. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and his chariots rush forward and destroy everything, as a storm does]
The pronoun **he** refers to the enemy who is coming to invade Judah. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [like clouds the enemy comes up]

The point of this comparison is that just as **eagles** fly very swiftly, so the enemy’s **horses** will move very swiftly. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [His horses move with extreme swiftness]

Jeremiah is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of despair. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How terrible it is for us, for we are destroyed]

The expression **we are devastated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for our enemies have devastated us]

14.note: Jeremiah is speaking of **evil** as if it were dirt that the people of Jerusalem could wash out of themselves. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Remove evil from your inner being]

The word **your** is singular here because Jeremiah is addressing the city of **Jerusalem** as if it were one person, but he means all of the people who live there. Use the form in your translation that your language would naturally use to address a group of people.

Jeremiah is speaking of the thoughts and the intentions of the people of Jerusalem as if they were contained in their **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your thoughts and desires]

The expression **you might be saved** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [so that Yahweh might save you]

Jeremiah is using the question form to rebuke the people of Jerusalem for holding on to their **wicked thoughts**. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Your wicked thoughts have remained within you for far too long!]

Jeremiah is speaking of the **wicked thoughts** of the people of Jerusalem as if they were guests who would **lodge** in their homes. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [will your wicked thoughts remain within you]

15.note: The word translated as **For** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [This is because]

Here, **a voice** represents the messenger who is speaking. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [a messenger declares]

The implication is that **Dan** and **the mount of Ephraim** lie to the north of Jerusalem, so the reports of the coming **disaster** trace the route by which the enemy army will advance. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from Dan in the far north … from the mount of Ephraim, nearer to Jerusalem, along the invaders’ route]

16.note: Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [Report this message to the nations: Look at what is about to happen]

Yahweh is using the term **Behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Look]

This is the beginning of what Yahweh says is to be announced to the nations and to Jerusalem. You may wish to mark the words of this speech with a first-level quotation mark at the beginning and end of them or with some other punctuation or convention that your language uses to indicate a first-level quotation.

The implication is that these **Guards** are the soldiers of the enemy army who will surround Jerusalem and besiege it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Enemy soldiers are coming from the distant land to besiege the city]

Yahweh is using **give their voice** as a common expression of the culture to mean “shout a war cry.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and they raise a war cry against the cities of Judah]

17.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **the watchmen of a field** station themselves all around a field to guard it, so the enemy soldiers will station themselves all around Jerusalem so that no one can escape. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [They will surround her completely, just as guards station themselves all around a field to keep watch over it]
The pronoun **her** refers to the city of Jerusalem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [they will be all around against Jerusalem]

18.note: Yahweh is speaking of **your way and your deeds** as if they were living things that could act and bring these disasters upon the people of Judah. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [you have brought these things on yourself because of the way you have lived and the things you have done]

The terms **way** and **deeds** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [your own habitual deeds]
The pronoun **these** refers to the disasters that Yahweh has just described. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [have brought these disasters on you]

Yahweh is speaking of the suffering that the people of Judah will experience as if it were food with a **bitter** taste. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Indeed it is very painful]

Yahweh is speaking of the innermost being of the people of Judah as if it were their **heart**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Indeed it reaches as far as your innermost being]

19.note: Jeremiah is using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of anguish. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [Oh, my anguish! Oh, my anguish]

Jeremiah is speaking of his **heart** as if it were a chamber that had **walls**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the strongest part of my heart]

Jeremiah is using **My heart is turbulent for me** as a common expression of the culture to mean “my heart is pounding wildly.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [My heart is pounding wildly]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **silent**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [I must speak out]

Jeremiah is speaking to his own **soul**, which cannot answer him. He is doing this to communicate to the people listening to him that he feels very strongly about the war that is coming. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate these words as if he were speaking directly to the people about himself. Alternate translation: [I tell you]

20.note: Jeremiah is using **Collapse upon collapse** as a common expression of the culture to mean “one disaster after another.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [One disaster after another is announced]

The expression **is called out** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [People loudly announce many collapses]

The expression **all the land is devastated** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [for enemies have devastated all the land]

Jeremiah is speaking of the homes of the people of Judah as if they were all **tents** with **curtains** hanging inside them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Suddenly my people’s homes are destroyed, in a moment, everything in them]

Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [in a moment, my curtains are devastated]

21.note: Jeremiah is using the question form to lament that the fighting goes on and on. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [For far too long I see the banner and hear the sound of the enemy’s horn!]

Here, **the banner** and **the sound of the horn** represent the war itself, since these are the signals that armies use in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [will I see battles, will I hear the noise of warfare]

Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [until when will I hear the sound of the horn]

22.note: This is the beginning of what Yahweh says about his people, although Jeremiah does not use a phrase to introduce the quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of indicating direct quotations in your language. See the UST.

Yahweh is using **know** as a common expression of the culture to mean “acknowledge and obey.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they do not acknowledge me as their God]

Here the masculine term **sons** has a generic sense that includes both men and women. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use language in your translation that is clearly inclusive of both men and women. Alternate translation: [foolish children]

22.q: בָּנִ֤ים סְכָלִים֙ הֵ֔מָּה וְ⁠לֹ֥א נְבוֹנִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה
22.note: Yahweh is speaking of his people as if they were **foolish** children who had not yet learned anything. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They are ignorant people who have learned nothing]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **understanding**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and they do not understand anything]

22.q: חֲכָמִ֥ים הֵ֨מָּה֙ לְ⁠הָרַ֔ע וּ⁠לְ⁠הֵיטִ֖יב לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ
22.note: Yahweh actually means to communicate the opposite of the literal meaning of what he is saying here. If a speaker of your language would not do that, you could translate the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [They are experts at doing evil, but they have no skill for doing good]

23.note: This could mean: (1) that he saw the whole earth. Alternate translation: [I saw the firmament that God had made] or (2) that Jeremiah saw **the land** of Judah. Alternate translation: [I looked into the promised land] You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers.

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and listen to me]

The terms **formless** and **empty** mean similar things. Jeremiah is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [it was completely desolate]

Jeremiah is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I looked to the heavens]

24.note: Jeremiah is using the pronoun **themselves** to emphasize how violently **all the hills** were trembling. Use a way that is natural in your language to indicate this emphasis.

Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And look]

25.note: Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [and listen]

Jeremiah is not referring to a specific **man**. He means human beings in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [there were no human beings]

26.note: Jeremiah is using the term **behold** to focus his listeners’ attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [listen again]

The implication is that **the orchard** stands for the fertile farmland of Judah, which had become as barren as **the wilderness**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the fertile farmland had become as barren as a wilderness]

The expression **had been pulled down** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and all the cities had collapsed]

Jeremiah is using **before the face of** as a common expression of the culture to mean “because of,” and he is using **his nose** as a common expression to refer to Yahweh’s anger. If these phrases do not have those meanings for your readers, you could use comparable expressions from your language that do have those meanings, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [because of Yahweh, because of his fierce anger]

27.q: שְׁמָמָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה כָּל־הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ וְ⁠כָלָ֖ה לֹ֥א אֶעֱשֶֽׂה
27.note: Yahweh says **All the land** as an extreme statement for emphasis, since he says in the next line that he will not destroy the land completely. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [Nearly the whole land will become a devastation, but complete destruction I shall not make]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **a devastation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [All the land will become devastated]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **destruction**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [but I shall not completely destroy it]

28.note: Yahweh is speaking of **the land** and **the heavens** as if they were living things that could **mourn** and put on dark clothing for grief. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the land will be desolate, and the sky above will be dark]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **plans**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Because I have spoken what I have planned to do]

The expressions **will not regret** and **shall not turn away from it** mean similar things. Yahweh is using the two expressions together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [and will not change my mind at all]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative word **turn away**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and I will keep my plans and follow through with them]

The pronoun **it** refers to what Yahweh has decided and announced that he will do. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and I shall not turn away from what I have decided to do]

29.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **horseman** or **shooter of the bow**. He means the horsemen and the archers of the enemy army in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [horsemen and men shooting bows]

In this verse, the word **city** is singular in form, but it refers to all of the cities of Judah as a group. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the plural form of “city.” Alternate translation: [all the cities will flee]

Here, **city** represents the people who live in the city. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the people of every city will flee]

Yahweh says **Every city will be abandoned** as an extreme statement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [City after city will be left empty, with hardly anyone still living in them]

The expression **will be abandoned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [The people will desert every city]

30.note: Yahweh is using the question form to assert that nothing the people of Jerusalem do will save them. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [devastated one, there is nothing that you can do!]

30.q: כִּֽי־תִלְבְּשִׁ֨י שָׁנִ֜י כִּי־תַעְדִּ֣י עֲדִי־זָהָ֗ב כִּֽי־תִקְרְעִ֤י בַ⁠פּוּךְ֙ עֵינַ֔יִ⁠ךְ לַ⁠שָּׁ֖וְא תִּתְיַפִּ֑י
30.note: Yahweh uses the word **Although** here to indicate a contrast between the great efforts that the people of Jerusalem make to beautify themselves and the worthless result that those efforts will achieve. In your translation, indicate this contrast in a way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [You may dress in scarlet, you may adorn yourself with jewelry of gold, you may enlarge your eyes with eye paint, but you beautify yourself for futility]

30.q: כִּֽי־תִלְבְּשִׁ֨י שָׁנִ֜י כִּי־תַעְדִּ֣י עֲדִי־זָהָ֗ב כִּֽי־תִקְרְעִ֤י בַ⁠פּוּךְ֙ עֵינַ֔יִ⁠ךְ
30.note: Yahweh is speaking of the people of Jerusalem as if they were a woman who put on **scarlet** clothing and **jewelry of gold** and **eye paint** in order to attract lovers. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Although you try to make yourself attractive to the nations, although you seek to win their favor with your splendor and wealth]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe **jewelry** that is characterized by being made of **gold**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [with golden jewelry]

The term **eye paint** refers to a dark cosmetic that women in this culture spread around their eyes to make their eyes look larger. If your readers would not be familiar with what eye paint is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [with dark makeup]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **futility**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [you beautify yourself, but it will do you no good]

Yahweh is speaking of the nations that had been allies of Judah as if they were men **lusting** after a woman. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Your former allies who pretended to love you now reject you]

Yahweh is using **seek your life** as a common expression of the culture to mean “try to kill you.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they are trying to kill you]

31.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a woman in labor** cries out from severe pain, so the people of Jerusalem will cry out from severe **distress**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [I hear a sound of severe pain, as loud as the cries a woman makes when she is giving birth to her first child, and anguish that intense]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [I hear distress like the distress of a woman birthing her firstborn]

Yahweh is using **the daughter of Zion** as a common expression to refer to the people who live in Jerusalem. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the people of Jerusalem]

Spreading out the **hands** was a symbolic action by which a person in this culture pleaded desperately for help. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [She spreads out her hands to plead desperately for help]

If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [And cries out that she is in great trouble, for she is fainting because of murderers]

The people of Jerusalem are using a phrase that expresses a strong feeling of despair. There may be an equivalent word or phrase in your language that you can use in your translation to convey this feeling. Alternate translation: [How terrible it is for me now]
Here, **my soul** represents the whole person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [I faint]
